sources.citation: sil.org site search result pages for 'Woria', 'Yoki', 'Tefaro', 'Waropen', 'Wordlist Jones', 'Botawa' (SIL Language & Culture Archives)
sources.note: Zero hits for Woria/Yoki/Botawa; neighbouring hits are 'Tefaro Wordlist Jones' (1987, archives/69265), 'Tefaro Wordlist Bouwman-Holster' (1985, 69149), 'Awera Wordlist in Wapoga Village in 1987' (57825) and 'Phonology of the Barapasi language' (98059). No Woria wordlist or report is archived online.
No Woria entry (Geelvink Bay entries: Barapasi, Bauzi, Demisa, Kehu, Tunggare).

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane A. 1997. Toward a reconstruction and reclassification of the Lakes Plain languages of Irian Jaya. In Franklin (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics 2, 133-236. Pacific Linguistics A-85. (held as../iauu1242/)
sources.note: Mentions Botawa only as the village of the Saponi wordlist; East Geelvink Bay membership deferred to Silzer & Clouse 1991 ('Bauzi, Demisa, etc.'). Nothing on Woria.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. (held as../awyi1241/)
sources.note: Woria is not listed; East Geelvink Bay stock-level family contains only Tarunggare, Baropasi, Bauri (pp. 51-52). Nothing on stress.
Nothing; says Woria is 'too poorly attested to be sure' of its classification; cites Ethnologue 22 and points to PARADISEC CLV1.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and md.ini for Woria (wori1246); family page geel1240
sources.note: Nothing; 0 descriptive references (refs: Jones 1987 overview, Sugono 2008 overview, Ethnologue 2009, Moseley 2010, WOLP).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Palmer, Bill (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide, 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (section on the East Cenderawasih Bay family)

sources.note: Most recent family-level overview of East Geelvink/Cenderawasih Bay; would confirm whether anything beyond Jones's wordlist exists for Woria and gives the family's prosodic profile (Bauzi pitch accent) -- second-hand at best for Woria.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2007. Australasia and the Pacific. In Moseley, Christopher (ed.), Encyclopedia of the world's endangered languages, 425-577. London: Routledge. Entry 'Woria'.

sources.note: Source of the '5-6 speakers (2000 Wurm)' figure; full entry seen only as a snippet. Endangerment note, almost certainly silent on phonology.

sources.citation: Silzer, Peter J. & Heljä Heikkinen Clouse. 1991. Index of Irian Jaya languages. 2nd edition. Jayapura: Program Kerjasama Universitas Cenderawasih and Summer Institute of Linguistics.

sources.note: The listing Clouse 1997 defers to for East Geelvink Bay membership; would show what SIL held on Woria c. 1991 (location, speaker count, wordlist provenance). Listing only; no phonology expected.

sources.citation: Jones, Larry B. 1987. The linguistic situation in the East Cenderawasih Bay, Irian Jaya: a preliminary survey. Unpublished survey report, SIL Papua (Jayapura). 10 pp. -- plus the accompanying 1987 Woria survey wordlist (Botawa), if it survives in the SIL Indonesia branch archive.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only first-hand source on Woria known to Glottolog; a survey overview is unlikely to state stress, but a phonetically transcribed wordlist with stress marks would be the only possible evidence. SIL archives the sister Tefaro/Awera wordlists from the same trip online but no Woria item.
